At the end of our street, there was a tree that held on to its leaves longer than the others. Every November, the maples stood bare while the oak kept a few brown leaves, dry and curled, through the first snow.

My neighbor called it stubborn. My father said some trees were simply built that way.

One windy afternoon, I stood beneath it and watched a leaf struggle on its stem. I was sure it would fall before I reached home, so I waited. The wind rattled every branch. A delivery truck passed. Someone called a dog.

The leaf stayed.

When I went by the next morning, it was gone. I looked for it on the sidewalk, though I had no idea how I’d recognize it among all the others.
